title: Current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August: RBI data
summary: India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data rele...
fullText:
India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data released by the RBI on Thursday.
The net deficit in the merchandise trade account declined to USD 26.6 billion in August from USD 27.6 billion in the same month last year.
Merchandise exports rose to USD 44.7 billion in August from USD 35.1 billion a year ago, while imports increased to USD 71.3 billion from USD 62.7 billion, the RBI data showed.
The surplus in services trade increased to USD 16.5 billion in August from USD 15.6 billion a year ago. Services exports rose to USD 35.5 billion from USD 31.2 billion, while imports increased to USD 18.9 billion from USD 15.6 billion.
Net transfers, including remittances, increased to USD 12.8 billion in August from USD 12.2 billion a year ago, while the net deficit in the income account widened to USD 8 billion from USD 6.3 .

No form of technology should be "artificially paused" and the need is to stay vigilant and think ahead on how to work with AI, so that innovation isn't stifled while the right governance and usage are built around it, IBM India and South Asia Managing Director Sandip Patel said on Tuesday.
In an interview to PTI, Patel said IBM India has always been a critical part of global operations, not only because the company continues to participate in the growth market here, but also because it is a "hotbed of innovation".
Innovations from India can be scaled and applied anywhere in the world, he said, pointing to Indian innovations such as UPI.
Citing a specific IBM innovation, Patel said the company was "very privileged" to be a part of the creation of YONO, the digital platform run by SBI. He called it a fairly unique proposition that has emerged from India and can be applied around the world.

title: US soccer fandom jumps to 75.2 million after World Cup 2026: Nielsen report
summary: Nielsen's Fan Insights data showed that US soccer fandom grew 27 per cent between 2022 and 2026, adding 16 million fans over five years
fullText: The number of American soccer fans increased to 75.2 million in July 2026, up from 66.8 million a year earlier, according to new data from research conducted by American firm Nielsen. The increase of 8.4 million fans comes in the aftermath of the FIFA World Cup 2026, suggesting that the tournament's popularity is translating into broader interest in the sport across the United States. Nielsen's Fan Insights data showed that US soccer fandom grew 27 per cent between 2022 and 2026, adding 16 million fans over five years. The rise in interest is also extending to domestic and international football competitions, with Major League Soccer (MLS), the Premier League and LaLiga recording increased viewership among younger audiences. The figures suggest that the World Cup has helped expand the sport's reach beyond the international tournament itself.US soccer fandom grows by 8.4 million in one yearAccording to Nielsen's proprietary Fan Insights data, the number of people identifying as soccer fans in the United States rose from 66.8 million in July 2025 to 75.2 million in July 2026. The year-on-year increase of 8.4 million indicates a growing audience for the sport following the 2026 World Cup. Over the five-year period from 2022 to 2026, US soccer fandom increased by 27 per cent, representing an additional 16 million fans. This expansion suggests that interest in the sport has been building over time, with the World Cup providing a major platform to introduce soccer to new audiences and strengthen engagement among existing supporters. The growth also presents an opportunity for broadcasters, clubs and competition organisers to convert tournament-driven interest into regular viewership and sustained fan engagement. ALSO READ: Indian Super League 2026-27 garners 65 million YouTube views in first weekMLS, Premier League and LaLiga viewership risesThe increase in soccer fandom has coincided with higher television audiences for several major competitions. Nielsen reported that regular-season MLS audiences on FOX and FS1 increased by 55 per cent among men aged 18-34 and 29 per cent among adults aged 18-34 after the league resumed following the World Cup break. The comparison was against regular-season matches played before the tournament. The Premier League also recorded a 30 per cent increase in viewership among adults aged 18-34 on NBC and USA Network, including Spanish-language broadcasts. The figures point to increased interest in European club football among younger American audiences. LaLiga viewership across ESPN, ESPN2, ABC and ESPN Deportes rose 42 per cent year-on-year across English- and Spanish-language broadcasts. Among viewers aged 18-34, the increase was even higher at 60 per cent. Together, the figures indicate that the increased attention surrounding the World Cup is extending to regular-season football, giving broadcasters and leagues an opportunity to build a larger audience in the US market.MLS fandom adds 11.7 million fans in five yearsNielsen's Fan Insights data also showed that MLS fandom increased by 28 per cent between 2022 and 2026, adding 11.7 million fans to the league's potential audience. The growth in MLS fandom comes as the domestic competition seeks to strengthen its position in a sports market traditionally dominated by American football, basketball, baseball and ice hockey. A larger potential audience offers MLS clubs and commercial partners opportunities to attract new supporters, expand their reach and build stronger connections with younger viewers. The rise in viewership among adults aged 18-34 across MLS and European leagues is particularly significant because regular-season audiences are important to sustaining interest beyond major international tournaments. Whether this momentum continues will depend partly on the ability of leagues and broadcasters to retain viewers throughout their respective seasons. Seth Ladetsky, global head of sports at Nielsen, said the World Cup had acted as a catalyst for soccer's growth across North America. He added that the data showed fandom reaching new highs while expanding among younger and diverse audiences and extending to major domestic and international leagues.How FIFA World Cup 2026 panned outThe 2026 edition of the FIFA World Cup was hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico from June 11 to July 19, making it the first edition to feature 48 teams and 104 matches across 16 host cities. The tournament concluded with Spain defeating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, securing Spain's second men's World Cup title. The expanded format brought more teams into the competition and added a round of 32 to the knockout stage. Matches were played across the three host nations, with Mexico City hosting the opening fixture and the United States staging the final. The tournament also drew a record total attendance of 6,810,966 spectators, according to FIFA.
author: Aditya Kaushik

title: Slower deliveries key to West Indies' win in 4th T20I, says Keemo Paul
summary: West Indies bowled out India for 223 after posting 247 for three and Paul marshalled the tourists' defence with a five-wicket haul on Wednesday
fullText: Pacer Keemo Paul said the West Indies bowlers employed slow balls to maximum effect on a slightly gripping pitch during their 24-run win over India in the fourth T20I here.West Indies bowled out India for 223 after posting 247 for three and Paul marshalled the tourists' defence with a five-wicket haul on Wednesday."From the batters' perspective, the message we got after the first five overs was that it was a pretty good wicket. One or two balls were gripping, but other than that, it was pretty good," Paul said in the post-match press conference."As bowlers, the slower balls helped us here. On other wickets and at other grounds, we haven't been getting much grip, but it worked here," he added.Paul struck at crucial stages of India's chase, dismissing Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prince Yadav off successive deliveries before removing Axar Patel to seal the West Indies' victory."The game plan was to keep bowling into the wicket for as long as possible and execute our yorkers when we knew they were going for the big shots." Paul said the absence of dew also made a difference, as bowlers could grip the ball better under lights."Some pretty big scores have been chased in this series, but I think a key factor is that there was no dew (in Hyderabad). When there is dew, it becomes quite hard for teams bowling second."In the last game and this one, there was no dew, and I think we executed our plans perfectly," he said.Paul credited captain Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and the partnerships he built for giving the bowlers enough runs to defend.Shimron Hetmyer made 33 off 12 deliveries, while Sherfane Rutherford remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls as the visitors posted a formidable total."Every game is the same for us. Whether we are batting first or batting second, we try to be as positive as possible. On these wickets, you have to score big. We did not win the toss today."But I think Captain Hope has been fantastic for us. The key partnerships he built gave us the runs we needed. I think the team bowled really well," Paul said.The 28-year-old said detailed team meetings and clarity over individual plans helped him execute his role under pressure."Every team has its own game plans. We sit together and discuss them, and we have some pretty long team meetings."I knew what I wanted to do, what my field settings would be and what my plan was. Obviously, I won't share my plan, but I think I executed it pretty well," he said.The pacer also acknowledged the challenge of bowling in T20 cricket, where the margin for error is small on batting-friendly pitches."You can't be too hard on yourself as a bowler on these tracks. The margin for error is very, very thin. It all comes down to execution. It is about taking it one day at a time and sticking to the process."As long as you try to follow the team's plans as much as possible, I don't think the staff will have a problem. You can't be too tough on yourself on these wickets," he said.

title: Samson defends bowlers after WI loss, says Tilak's wicket proved costly
summary: India were bowled out for 223 in 19.3 overs after the West Indies posted 247 for three, with Shai Hope smashing an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and Keemo Paul claiming a five-wicket haul
fullText: Sanju Samson on Wednesday defended India's bowlers after their 24-run defeat to the West Indies in the fourth T20, saying the emerging pacers will improve with experience while identifying Tilak Varma's dismissal as the turning point of their failed chase.India were bowled out for 223 in 19.3 overs after the West Indies posted 247 for three, with Shai Hope smashing an unbeaten 102 off 50 balls and Keemo Paul claiming a five-wicket haul to level the five-match series at 2-2.Samson said India has no replacement for the rested Jasprit Bumrah, describing the pace spearhead as a once-in-a-generation bowler, but backed the emerging fast bowlers to improve with experience and opportunities."He is a once-in-a-generation bowler, and we are very lucky to have him. But we also have some really good talent coming through. Arshdeep has been doing a great job, and the way Prince Yadav has bowled in the last few games has been very impressive."We have some really good quality talent, and the more we play them and back them, the more matches we give them, the better they will become," Samson said.India's bowling struggled to contain the West Indies, with Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh conceding 52 runs each in their four overs. Arshdeep was also struck on the left bicep by a short delivery from Shamar Joseph in the final over of India's chase and left the field after receiving medical attention.Samson praised Hope for his match-defining knock, saying the West Indies skipper had batted with control."He has been playing really well, and we need to respect what he has been doing. He has been playing some really good cricketing shots without taking too many risks."We have to give him credit for the way he is batting, and we are definitely working on how to respond to him in every game," he said.Samson said Hyderabad's conditions offered good bounce and were conducive to high-scoring T20 cricket."Coming to Hyderabad, we know we get good bounce on the track and that the games can be high-scoring. That has been a constant feature of this series." He cited the Lucknow game, where the surface offered assistance to bowlers, as an example of how batting plans need to change according to conditions."When you are playing on a high-scoring ground, you have to go into fifth gear from ball one. But if you are playing on a surface where the scores are around 160-170, like in the Lucknow game, where there was something in the wicket, your plans change accordingly."You cannot always play the same kind of cricket. You have to assess the conditions, the bounce and the situation," Samson said.Chasing 248, India made a blistering start through Samson, who smashed 56 off 23 balls, including six fours and four sixes, as the hosts raced to 60 without loss in four overs.However, Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over to remove Samson and Ishan Kishan, before the West Indies tightened their grip on the contest.Samson said the dismissal of Tilak, who scored 43 off 25 deliveries, proved decisive as India were still in contention at that stage."I think the turning point was when Tilak got out. As I said, we were cruising along nicely. Reddy and Tilak were putting the bowlers under pressure and batting really well." Samson also backed Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma, saying one match should not overshadow their performances at the top of the order."I think Ishan and Abhishek Sharma are two of the best batters in the world at the top of the order. You cannot really ask for more from them. One game (not scoring) is fine." Samson acknowledged the visitors' performance ahead of Saturday's series decider in Bengaluru."We are 2-2 now, and everything comes down to the game in Bengaluru. We are very charged up and want to go out there and compete against them. West Indies have been playing some really good cricket, and you have to give them credit for coming to India and dominating in two games," he said.
author: Press Trust of India

title: Mourinho receives 'eternal glory' from Roma fans on return with Real Madrid
summary: Even before the coach walked out into the Stadio Olimpico ahead of kickoff for a Champions League match, there was a long applause when the stadium announcer read out the teams and Mourinho's name
fullText: Jose Mourinho was treated like a returning hero when he brought Real Madrid to face Roma, one of his many former clubs, on Wednesday.And he snatched the victory, too, as Madrid came back from two goals down for a 4-3 win with three goals in the final 10 minutes - with all three scores following corner kicks.Even before the coach walked out into the Stadio Olimpico ahead of kickoff for a Champions League match, there was a long applause when the stadium announcer read out the teams and Mourinho's name.Then early in the first half, the end of the stadium where Roma's hard-core "ultra" fans sit held up three huge signs featuring images of Mourinho - one of which depicted him cradling the Conference League trophy that Roma won in 2022 to conclude his first season in charge.The Conference title was Roma's first significant European trophy.Mourinho also led Roma to the Europa League final in 2023. He left the club in January 2024 without really saying goodbye."Whoever brings glory to Rome, Rome will honor forever," read a fans' banner. "The people bestow you with eternal glory." Mourinho said he was left "speechless" by the reception.In return, Mourinho didn't celebrate when late goals from Carlos Espi, Endrick and Antonio Rudiger turned the match around."You could say there were two games in one," Mourinho said. "Roma was better in all aspects early on. ... When it was 3-1 everyone probably thought the game was dead. But it was the Roma players who were dead." The result was a welcome reprieve for Mourinho, who has been waging a vocal campaign against the Spanish league referees.Earlier Wednesday, Madrid forward Vinicius Junior was banned for four league matches, including the "clasico" against Barcelona, after pulling the hair of an opponent in Saturday's 1-0 win over Villarreal.Madrid is in fourth place in the Spanish league and already trails perfect Barcelona by six points.Mourinho's criticism of the referees has drawn the ire of Spanish league president Javier Tebas.It was the second straight Champions League match that Mourinho faced one of his former Italian clubs, after Madrid hung on for a 2-1 win over Inter Milan last month after scoring two early goals.

title: Vinicius handed four-game ban; set to miss Clasico after hair-pulling row
summary: Vinicius was shown a straight red card in the 73rd minute for having tugged hard on the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba when they were sprinting down the field
fullText: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior has been banned for four league matches, including the "clasico" against Barcelona, after pulling the hair of an opponent in Saturday's 1-0 win over Villarreal.Vinicius was shown a straight red card in the 73rd minute for having tugged hard on the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba when they were sprinting down the field, moments before the Madrid player scored a goal. The goal was also ruled out.The Spanish soccer federation's disciplinary committee announced the four-match suspension shortly before Madrid's Champions League match at Roma on Wednesday. Madrid came from two goals down to snatch a 4-3 win in the Italian capital and coach Jose Mourinho slammed the timing of the announcement afterwards."Do you think it's normal for a player from a Spanish team, preparing for an important match that's also crucial for Spanish soccer, to find out about his four-match suspension just two hours before kickoff?" Mourinho said."Couldn't they have announced the decision now or tomorrow morning? We were on the bus about to arrive at the stadium when we found out. They've started doing things without any shame." Real Madrid was expected to appeal the suspension. Spanish media said an initial appeal had already been dismissed.The committee said Vinicius was banned for two matches for the hair pulling and a further two matches for his subsequent aggressive protests to referee Isidro Diaz de Mera.Vinicius screamed at Diaz de Mera while his teammates tried to calm him down as he left the field.Diaz de Mera wrote in his match report that after being shown the red card Vinicius "protested my decision, raising his voice, toward where I was standing in an aggressive manner, and being held back by teammates." Vinicius will miss Sunday's home match against Sevilla and the following week's trip to Barcelona. He will also miss away matches at Racing Santander and Valencia.
author: AP

title: PSG humble Man City after pre-match defiance in Champions League clash
summary: Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha all scored and the defending champion created numerous other chances to secure the win
fullText: Manchester City wowed fans with a spectacular fireworks show and a highlights reel of some of its greatest hits before the Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain.It quickly went downhill from there.In what could be interpreted as a latest display of defiance from the embattled club - which has been found guilty of widespread financial wrongdoing - City produced a slick pre-match show reminding supporters of the good times with footage of its most iconic moments on the Etihad Stadium's big screens.On the field, however, the highlights belonged to PSG in a blistering first-half performance, which saw the back-to-back European champion race to a 3-0 lead at the break, including two goals in quick succession.And even if City mounted a spirited second-half fightback, a 4-2 loss brought the club down to earth after the triumphalism that some found off-putting in the wake of Sunday's 3-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool."Against this kind of team it's already difficult when you are 0-0 and and then in two minutes you concede two goals, probably we lost a little bit of balance," City coach Enzo Maresca said. "I think we can learn many things. First of all even if we concede two goals against probably the best team in Europe in this moment, we need to continue to do the right things." With former City manager Pep Guardiola watching on from the stands, PSG's first-half blitz sobered the atmosphere after the rousing pre-match show.Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha all scored and the defending champion created numerous other chances to extend its lead.This was City's first home game since an independent panel found that it broke Premier League rules by artificially inflating its revenue by more than $1 billion over nearly a decade on its way to dominating English soccer.City has appealed, leaving an air of uncertainty over the club's future and the season as a whole, with potential punishments including a huge fine, points deductions or even expulsion from England's top flight.The Emirati-owned City has always pleaded its innocence and along with its fans has been resolute in its determination to clear its name.This was the first chance to put on a show of solidarity at its home stadium since the verdict.A huge banner was hung with the words: "I know I am, I'm sure I am, I'm City til I die".The highlight reel included Sergio Aguero's famous title-winning goal in 2012 as well as other moments predating the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008.In the stands, Guardiola - on his first return to the club since stepping down at the end of last season - sat behind club chief executive Ferran Soriano.Despite the verdict, City has refused to be bowed and the win against Liverpool was evidence its players could put the outside noise to one side and focus on the field.PSG, however, was different story.Another club that has benefited wildly from investment from the Middle East through its Qatari backers, the French giant has built the finest team in Europe and lived up to that billing by sweeping City aside in the first half.It was the type of performance to suggest it is capable of a Champions League three-peat, emulating the all-time king of Europe Real Madrid.At the break it felt like City could be on the end of a humbling defeat.However, Enzo Maresca's team managed to turn a would-be rout into a thrilling clash.Erling Haaland scored two goals, two efforts came back off the woodwork and another chance was cleared off the line.Maghnes Akliouche's goal, in between Haaland's, effectively ensured there would be no comeback and Ferran Torres then failed to score a fifth for the visitors from the penalty spot."It's not important to be the best in the competition now, it's important to be the best in the final," PSG coach Luis Enrique said.

title: Messi helps Inter Miami clinch MLS playoff berth with 2-0 win over NYCFC
summary: Miami missed the postseason when Messi arrived in 2023, but has reached the playoffs the past three seasons
fullText: Rodrigo De Paul scored on an assist from Lionel Messi and German Berterame added a goal to send reigning champion Inter Miami back to the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over New York City FC on Wednesday night.Luis Suarez also assisted for Inter Miami, which has won back-to-back matches for the first time since July.Miami missed the postseason when Messi arrived in 2023, but has reached the playoffs the past three seasons, losing in the first round to Atlanta United in 2024 then beating Vancouver last year to win the club's first MLS Cup.Wednesday's victory came after Miami routed DC United 4-0 last Saturday on a pair of goals from Messi and Suarez, and it was the second league win for new coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez, who took over Sept. 16.Berterame scored in the 20th for his eighth goal of the season. De Paul doubled Miami's lead right before the end of the first half. Dayne St. Clair denied Nicolas Fernandez on a penalty in the final minute of the match for his second straight clean sheet.It has been a rollercoaster year for Messi, who led Argentina to its second straight World Cup final and announced his retirement from international soccer a month later. Now, he has a chance to cap it with another trophy.

title: Iyer stresses better execution and fresh mindset after T20I loss vs WI
summary: India skipper Shreyas Iyer on Wednesday stressed the need for better execution and the right mindset going forward after the hosts suffered a 24-run defeat against the West Indies in the fourth T20I here.
fullText: India skipper Shreyas Iyer on Wednesday stressed the need for better execution and the right mindset going forward after the hosts suffered a 24-run defeat against the West Indies in the fourth T20I here.India's innings ended at 223/9 in 19.3 overs after Arshdeep Singh retired hurt while chasing the West Indies' imposing total of 247 for three, allowing the visitors to level the five-match series 2-2.The series decider will be played at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on Saturday."It all started with bowling. We didn't execute our line and lengths well and, at the end of the day, when you're chasing 250, you have to go about it in a certain pattern," Iyer said."I liked our approach during the chase, but we were unfortunate that we couldn't execute our plans with the ball, and that's where we fell a bit short." "They executed their plans well, and there was a bit of assistance from the wicket as well. The ball was kicking up, and they used the field pretty well. So, credit where it's due - their execution was spot on," Iyer added.He continued, "The approach is going to be the same, and I feel that going forward, we don't have to think too much about our bowling. It's all about execution and having a fresh mindset, where you come out on a given day, execute your plans and seize the moment." Iyer said the series-deciding fifth T20I would be an "interesting" contest."Even though the momentum shifted towards us in between, their ability to bounce back was top-notch, and I'm sure the fifth one will be an interesting contest," he said.West Indies skipper Shai Hope, who struck an unbeaten 102 for his second century in four matches in the series, said his team's total was competitive, given the nature of the pitch at the Uppal Stadium."I honestly felt it was a decent score because the surface was actually holding up a bit more than we initially thought. We felt the pitch would probably be a bit better for batting," Hope said."But I found that with the new ball, some deliveries were kicking up a lot more, while others were staying low as well. It was a bit two-paced to start with and then, obviously, with the spinners and the quicks at the back end, it became a little more difficult to hit through the line," he added.Keemo Paul, who returned figures of 5/41 to derail India's chase, said the West Indies bowlers stuck to their plans, keeping the nature of the pitch in mind."We have a simple plan: try to nail the yorkers and, if that doesn't work, go into the wicket. Obviously, the wicket assisted us a bit. The slower balls were gripping, so we just tried not to be too predictable," Paul said."We were up for the fight in this T20 tournament. I just want to contribute whenever I get the opportunity. It's not easy bowling on these wickets, but you have to back yourself. Tonight, I executed my plans, and I'm very happy about that," the bowler added.

title: BFI president and secretary general trade suspensions amid power tussle
summary: Kumar, in an earlier letter to the president, had stated that Pinnacle committed Rs two crore towards sponsorship and broadcasting of the event
fullText: The power struggle in the Boxing Federation of India intensified on Wednesday with president Ajay Singh and secretary general Pramod Kumar suspending each other, both alleging violations of the federation's constitution.Singh suspended Kumar on Tuesday pending an inquiry into alleged financial irregularities, non-cooperation with investigations and misuse of authority.On Wednesday, Kumar issued a counter-order suspending Singh pending the outcome of a no-confidence motion, which he had planned to move during a Special General Meeting (SGM) on October 28. He had claimed the support of a majority of affiliated state units to move the no-confidence motion.Kumar accused Singh of continuing to exercise executive control over the federation despite being served a cease-and-desist notice on October 8.However, Singh rejected his suspension, calling it "unauthorised and without constitutional basis"."The constitution does not confer an independent power on the Secretary General to suspend the President. BFI therefore rejects the claim that a letter issued solely under the Secretary General's authority can, by itself, suspend the sitting President," a BFI media release said.Allegations against Kumar "You are placed under interim suspension from the office of Secretary General with immediate effect, pending completion of the inquiry or until the order is modified or revoked by the competent authority, subject to the applicable provisions of the BFI Constitution," read the order against Kumar, in possession of PTI.The order, however, clarified that the suspension was an interim measure and "shall not be construed as a final determination of the allegations".In his order, Singh also accused Kumar failing to cooperate with an inquiry into the cancellation of a national championship and attempting to convene an unauthorised meeting to move a no-confidence motion against the president.In the BFI order, Singh alleged that the federation had received notices from Pinnacle Broadcast Productions seeking approximately Rs 1.5 crore for broadcasting undertaken at the World Boxing Finals Cup in Greater Noida in November last year.Kumar, in an earlier letter to the president, had stated that Pinnacle committed Rs two crore towards sponsorship and broadcasting of the event. But the company has denied making such a commitment."The Federation has recently received notices from Pinnacle Broadcast Productions making a claim for Rs. 1.5 crore (approx.) for broadcasting undertaken in the World Boxing Final's Cup, Greater Noida, November 2025."Whereas, the understanding as per the letter forwarded by you to the President was that Pinnacle had committed and assured Rs. 2 crore for the sponsorship and broadcasting of the event." "Pinnacle has now categorically denied making any such commitment, which raises serious doubt as to the authenticity of the letter that you personally represented Pinnacle had issued." The BFI order further alleged that a work order bearing Kumar's signature had been issued without the approval of the body's finance committee.Singh also cited an inquiry into the last-minute cancellation of the BFI Elite Men and Women Open Boxing Championship, scheduled to be held in Nahan, Himachal Pradesh, from August 16 to 23.An inquiry committee had been constituted on August 17 but Kumar had repeatedly sought more time and failed to respond to its questions.Another ground cited for the suspension was Kumar's alleged issuance of notices against senior federation officials and a communication seeking to convene a meeting to move a no-confidence motion against Singh."..instead of cooperating with the ongoing investigations, you have purported to issue cease-and-desist notices against senior officials of the BFI, show cause notices and a notice purporting to convene a meeting to move a no confidence motion against the President," the order read.It said Kumar had no authority under the BFI constitution to issue such notices without the requisite approval or to unilaterally convene SGMs.The order directed Kumar to refrain from exercising his functions as secretary general, issuing communications on behalf of the federation and accessing official records relevant to the inquiry.Kumar suspends BFI president pending no-confidence vote In his counter-order, Kumar accused Singh of treating the federation as his "fiefdom" and continuing to exercise executive control over its day-to-day administration despite a cease-and-desist notice."Being habitual of having almost no regard for the democratic set up and treating Boxing Federation of India as your fiefdom," Kumar wrote in the order, alleging that Singh's actions violated the federation's constitution and threatened the "sanctity and fair conduct" of the October 28 SGM.Citing allegations raised by affiliated state units, Kumar accused Singh of taking executive and policy decisions without mandatory approvals, attempting unauthorised constitutional amendments and threatening state associations with suspensions and ad hoc committees.Kumar further accused Singh of "willfully disregarding binding directions issued by the High Court of Delhi concerning election circulars, governance parameters, and tenure limits." Kumar's order stated that Singh's suspension would remain in force pending the final vote on the no-confidence motion at the October 28 SGM or further orders from the competent General Body.

title: ODI World Cup triumph not enough, India must work hard in T20Is: Mandhana
summary: Mandhana is set to lead India in her first assignment as full-time captain when the hosts take on Zimbabwe in a three-match T20I series starting here on Friday
fullText: Newly appointed captain Smriti Mandhana on Wednesday said India may have won the ODI World Cup recently, but the team still needs to work hard in the shortest format, with the inaugural edition of the Women's Champions Trophy set to be held early next year.India will host the six-team tournament in the T20 format at Mumbai's Brabourne Stadium and the BCA Stadium in Vadodara from February 14 to 28.Mandhana is set to lead India in her first assignment as full-time captain when the hosts take on Zimbabwe in a three-match T20I series starting here on Friday, followed by three ODIs in Vadodara. She took charge from Harmanpreet Kaur.Mandhana said India would look to make the most of the six T20Is ahead of the Women's Champions Trophy."The first bilateral (series) with Zimbabwe, I think, is very exciting. It is our first time playing with them," Mandhana told reporters here."Sometimes, playing with Zimbabwe and all the Associate nations, it feels like you can learn a lot from them as well because they enjoy playing their cricket."Sometimes, we get into a lot of things professionally. You can learn a lot from them. But again, we have six T20 matches before the Champions Trophy as an Indian team, so we will look to set standards as an Indian team (as to) how we approach the next three months leading up to the Champions Trophy," Mandhana added.Mandhana said there were several areas in which the Indian team needed to improve in the shortest format."We have won the World Cup in the last one-and-a-half years, but there were a few things which we needed to work on in the T20 format especially," she said."But I would say our strength has been the players who have come in. They have done extremely well. On the first day, I wouldn't really want to talk about weaknesses in a way."There are a lot of things we need to work on. We need a lot of things to get in place. But I think today is the day to talk about good and positive stuff," Mandhana said.Mandhana said she had been part of India's leadership group for a long time and that full-time captaincy would not be an entirely new challenge for her."I have been the vice-captain for the last almost 10 years. So, I have been part of the leadership role and I wouldn't say it is an extremely new thing. But for sure, it is something to look forward to and hopefully, I can do justice to the role," Mandhana said.The Indian captain expressed confidence in the young talent coming through the ranks."Jemimah (Rodrigues) has been injured for the last two months. (But) I think we have got exciting players. Anushka (Sharma) and Niki (Prasad), who have done really well in India A, and of course G Kamalini, who was No. 3 in the Asian Games," Mandhana said."We have a lot of options and I am really positive that they will do well," she added.Mandhana was part of a review meeting with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, head coach Amol Muzumdar and Harmanpreet Kaur a day before the former captain stepped down from the role across formats. Mandhana said the discussion centred on how to take Indian cricket forward."We had a meeting a day before. The conversation was about how to take Indian cricket forward," Mandhana replied when asked if she knew beforehand that she would be appointed captain." and what should be the approach for the next two to three years because we have a lot of major tournaments coming up," she added.Mandhana hoped the captaincy would have no impact on her batting."I have become a captain on the field; there should be no changes in my batting. My coach used to tell me when I was 15 years old, 'Whenever you bat, always think you are the captain'."You always take that responsibility, and those things have never changed. If the ball is in the zone, I will still go for it. I will still play whatever (way) the team needs (me) to," Mandhana added.

title: Sachin Tendulkar partners with OpenAI to drive wider adoption of ChatGPT
summary: Tendulkar announced the collaboration on X, saying he was looking forward to exploring new possibilities with ChatGPT and sharing what he found useful
fullText: Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has partnered with OpenAI to encourage more people to explore ChatGPT, sharing his experiences with the artificial intelligence tool and demonstrating how it can be used for everyday tasks, personal interests and preparation. The partnership will focus on discovering practical applications of the chatbot and helping people understand how it can be useful in areas they care about. Tendulkar announced the collaboration on X last month, saying he was looking forward to exploring new possibilities with ChatGPT and sharing what he found useful.  However, in a latest conversation with entrepreneur and content creator Varun Mayya, the former India captain explained how he was introduced to the chatbot while planning a family holiday and how he subsequently incorporated it into his preparation for travel, meetings and other engagements. Describing his experience with ChatGPT as a journey from curiosity to conviction, Tendulkar also discussed the role of technology in cricket, the importance of expertise and why access to information cannot replace practical experience.Sachin Tendulkar to showcase ChatGPT's practical applicationsTendulkar said his initial encounter with ChatGPT came shortly before his 50th birthday, when his family was planning a safari to Kenya's Maasai Mara. The itinerary involved flying to Nairobi, prompting him to seek information about aircraft safety and the journey. His brother, Ajit Tendulkar, suggested using ChatGPT to address his questions. The family eventually booked a flight, and the experience introduced the former cricketer to the chatbot's potential as a practical information tool. Since then, Tendulkar has used ChatGPT to prepare for travel, speaking engagements and meetings. He explained that he has always valued preparation, a habit he developed during his school days with his brother's guidance. The chatbot helps him organise his thoughts, identify relevant questions and approach conversations better prepared. Tendulkar's experience illustrates the approach he hopes to share through the partnership: encouraging people to begin with their own questions, interests and everyday requirements rather than treating AI as a technology that is difficult to understand. He has also experimented with using ChatGPT for personal interests. Tendulkar described working with friends to design a customised car, combining a colour unavailable as a standard option from the manufacturer with wheels from another brand. The exercise allowed the group to explore a configuration that a conventional car configurator might not have offered. ALSO READ: Virat Kohli makes Linkedin debut after choosing equity over endorsementHow cricket analytics changed Tendulkar's approach to the gameTendulkar's views on AI are informed partly by his experience of witnessing technology change cricket preparation during his playing career. He recalled the introduction of an analyst to the Indian team's dressing room during the 2002 tour of South Africa, when laptops, cameras and video footage began playing a greater role in training and team meetings. Initially unfamiliar with the technology, the players gradually recognised its value. Footage helped make net sessions more focused, while bowlers used analysis of individual batters to identify weaknesses and develop plans to exploit them. Tendulkar said the process made the team's approach, particularly to bowling, more scientific and precise. The experience demonstrated how technology could improve established methods when players were willing to adopt it and incorporate it into their preparation. The comparison also provides context for his current interest in ChatGPT. Just as video analysis helped cricketers examine performances more closely, AI tools can help users organise information, investigate questions and prepare for decisions. Their usefulness, however, depends on how effectively people apply the information they receive.Tendulkar says AI cannot replace expertise and hard workWhile acknowledging the benefits of AI, Tendulkar stressed that access to information does not automatically translate into expertise. Discussing the future role of specialists in a world where AI can provide answers across numerous fields, he maintained that experience and practical application would remain essential. He drew on his own relationship with his brother, who regularly provided feedback on his batting throughout his international career. Although those discussions helped him identify areas for improvement, Tendulkar still had to take the advice onto the field and work on the necessary changes himself. He viewed ChatGPT as a tool that could provide guidance comparable in some respects to the inputs of coaches and mentors, while emphasising that users could not bypass the effort required to develop a skill. The discussion also examined how AI could help reduce information gaps between experienced professionals and people entering unfamiliar fields. Mayya explained that users could turn to ChatGPT to identify questions they should ask, research unfamiliar subjects and make more informed decisions. For Tendulkar, the distinction is between making information accessible and developing the ability to use it effectively. The technology can support learning and preparation, but the responsibility for applying its output remains with the individual.OpenAI partnership comes amid expanding uses of AITendulkar's partnership with OpenAI comes as generative AI tools expand beyond answering questions to supporting research, planning, creative work and professional tasks. His examples of using ChatGPT for travel planning, meeting preparation and customised design offer practical illustrations of how the technology can fit into everyday routines. During his conversation with Mayya, Tendulkar also discussed the possibility of AI agents performing tasks on behalf of users. Mayya described a shift from systems that primarily respond to prompts towards tools capable of carrying out more complex activities, potentially freeing up time for other priorities. The discussion reflected the broader evolution of AI from an information resource towards technology that can assist with tasks. However, Tendulkar's emphasis remained on understanding how the tools can be used and combining their capabilities with human judgement and effort. Through the partnership, Tendulkar plans to explore further applications of ChatGPT, share his findings and encourage more people to try it for themselves. The focus, as outlined in his announcement, is on making the technology more approachable by connecting it with familiar interests and practical needs.

title: Netflix secures exclusive rights to broadcast 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain
summary: Under the arrangement, one match on every matchday will be available free of charge, while a national free-to-air broadcaster will show every Spain match
fullText: Netflix has secured exclusive rights to broadcast the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain, marking its first major broadcasting agreement for a men's World Cup. The streaming platform announced on Tuesday that it will carry all 104 matches of the 48-team tournament live, with Spain co-hosting the competition alongside Portugal and Morocco. The agreement also includes provisions for free-to-air coverage, ensuring viewers in Spain can watch selected matches without a subscription. Under the arrangement, one match on every matchday will be available free of charge, while a national free-to-air broadcaster will show every Spain match, both semi-finals and the final. The financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. The 2030 edition will mark 100 years since the inaugural men's World Cup in Uruguay in 1930. To commemorate the centenary, Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay will each host one match before the tournament continues across Spain, Portugal and Morocco.Netflix's 2030 FIFA World Cup deal: What does it include?Netflix will stream all 104 matches of the 2030 FIFA World Cup live in Spain under the exclusive rights agreement with FIFA. The deal gives the platform coverage of the entire tournament, including the group stage and knockout rounds. However, the arrangement also provides for free-to-air access to selected fixtures. Netflix has confirmed that one match per matchday will be available free in Spain. In addition, a national free-to-air broadcaster will be permitted to show all matches involving Spain, both semi-finals and the final. The agreement does not disclose the value of the rights package or the identity of the broadcaster that will carry the free-to-air matches. The deal marks Netflix's first major agreement for a men's FIFA World Cup, expanding its involvement in international football broadcasting beyond its existing commitments to the women's game.How will the 2030 FIFA World Cup be played?The 2030 FIFA World Cup will feature 48 teams competing across Spain, Portugal and Morocco, following an opening set of three matches in South America. As part of FIFA's centenary celebrations, Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay will each host one match. Uruguay staged the inaugural World Cup in 1930, making the South American fixtures part of the tournament's 100-year commemoration. After the opening three games, the competition will move to southern Europe and North Africa for the remainder of the tournament. Spain and Morocco are competing to host the final. The two countries have emerged as the leading candidates for the showpiece match, with the decision carrying significance for both national football administrations and their governments. The proposed venues include Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium and the King Hassan II Stadium near Casablanca, which is being built with a planned capacity of 115,000 spectators. ALSO READ: FIFA plans to double development funding; India could receive $25 millionNetflix expands FIFA broadcasting partnershipThe agreement for the 2030 men's tournament follows Netflix's 2024 deal with FIFA for the United States rights to the 2027 and 2031 Women's World Cups. The arrangement reflects the streaming platform's expanding presence in live sports broadcasting. The 2031 Women's World Cup is expected to be co-hosted by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, subject to FIFA's confirmation of the hosting arrangements. FIFA has traditionally awarded World Cup broadcasting rights to public broadcasters in many markets to maximise audience reach. The Spanish agreement with Netflix combines exclusive streaming access with a free-to-air provision for selected matches. The financial value of the 2030 deal has not been announced. For comparison, Spain's rights for the 2026 World Cup, which will be staged across North America, were awarded to public broadcaster RTVE for a reported €55 million (approximately $61.6 million).Where to watch the FIFA World Cup 2030 in India?In India, Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd (ZEEL) holds the official media rights to broadcast the 2030 FIFA World Cup under an eight-year, multi-tournament agreement running through 2034. The agreement covered the 2026 men's World Cup and will also cover the 2027 Women's World Cup, including a total of 39 FIFA events.

title: Ashwin says Bhuvneshwar's recall rewards success, not a reward he chased
summary: Bhuvneshwar's inclusion in India's squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning next week, was among the major talking points following the selection announcement
fullText: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar never had an India comeback on his mind while consistently delivering for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL, with the pacer's performances eventually earning him a recall to the national T20I squad after four years.Bhuvneshwar's inclusion in India's squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning next week, was among the major talking points following the selection announcement.Former India off-spinner Ashwin felt the experienced pacer concentrated on his responsibilities rather than worrying about the rewards that could follow his performances."I have a feeling that Bhuvneshwar Kumar hasn't even thought about a comeback. I think this will be his mantra for success. And when I'm watching him from afar, I have also experienced this myself, he has gone on his own journey," Ashwin said on his YouTube channel."He has focused on doing well, bowling well with the new ball and performing for RCB. Whatever he could do, he did it. His recall is the reward for his success. He never chased that reward; he simply did his job and success followed," he added.Bhuvneshwar's return has also triggered speculation over Mohammed Shami's international future. Ashwin, however, said a comeback remained possible for the senior pacer, provided he was prepared to put in the required effort."It depends on the cricketer. If a player has the belief that he can return, then they have to work hard towards it," said the 40-year-old, who has played 106 Tests for India.Ashwin also opened up about his relationships with Jasprit Bumrah and Virat Kohli, saying his equation with the former was largely built around light-hearted banter, while his bond with Kohli improved after the latter relinquished the captaincy."My relationship with Jassi is very good. We always joke and pull each other's legs. There isn't much conversation between us as cricketers, so our relationship is very banter-oriented," he said.On Kohli, Ashwin said their relationship became even better once the batting great was no longer leading the side and could focus solely on his role as a player.Looking ahead to the 2027 ODI World Cup, Ashwin backed India to be among the leading contenders but identified hosts South Africa as a formidable challenger in home conditions."India has the ability. If Jasprit Bumrah is firing on all cylinders, he will have a good fast-bowling experience. India has a good spin stock. There, in a lot of grounds, you will get the help of spin. There is experience in batting," he said.However, Ashwin rated South Africa highly, pointing to their familiarity with local conditions, the experience gained through the SA20 league and the team's overall cohesion."I will honestly say that two-three teams look good to me. Out of them, South Africa is the best. I think South Africa will be a serious contender for the home World Cup. So India will have to play against the South African team," he said."South Africa, in South African conditions, especially after SA20, have the skills, they know all the conditions, they play good cricket and the team looks together. That's a very strong force in cricket," Ashwin said.

title: Sammy says West Indies' powerplay struggles hurting them against India
summary: India lead the five-match series 2-1 ahead of the fourth T20 International here on Wednesday, with Sammy saying his side had repeatedly been forced to recover from expensive powerplays while bowling
fullText: West Indies need to win both powerplays to beat India in India, head coach Darren Sammy said on Tuesday, identifying the first six overs as the decisive phase in the ongoing T20I series while backing experienced all-rounder Roston Chase amid criticism over his place in the side.India lead the five-match series 2-1 ahead of the fourth T20 International here on Wednesday, with Sammy saying his side had repeatedly been forced to recover from expensive powerplays while bowling."I think the powerplay was the difference that prevented us from going 2-1 up, because we could have been 2-1 up as well," Sammy said.He pointed out that India had scored at nearly 14.5 runs per over in the powerplay, despite West Indies restricting the scoring rate to below 10 runs an over in each of the subsequent three phases."For us, it is about controlling the powerplay. So far, we have had to pull the game back every single time. That is an area we need to work on," he said."To beat India in India, you really have to win both powerplays, with bat and ball." Sammy felt West Indies' batting had matched India's in the series, with his side also striking more sixes in some matches. He said the visitors had looked to make the most of batting-friendly conditions, knowing that such surfaces were not always available."When you play on good batting wickets, you always feel you are in the game. You are just two big overs away from getting yourself back into it," he said.The challenge, he added, was greater for the bowlers, with little margin for error on surfaces where totals of 200 or more are common."The margins are fine, but as we have seen, if you execute your skills, you are still in the contest. We all understand that these are often 200-plus wickets. If 200 is a par score, you have to prevent the opposition from getting to 250," he said.Sammy cited India's skilful use of yorkers as an example of the execution required to contain batters. He also referred to assistant coach Ravi Rampaul's observation that hitting more fours than sixes could save two runs each time, and recalled Kimo Paul's description of bowling in such conditions: "Either you execute or you get executed." The West Indies coach also defended Chase, who has faced criticism over his continued selection, saying the all-rounder's discipline, tactical understanding and defensive mindset make him particularly valuable with the ball.Sammy also defended Chase, who has taken six wickets in the first three T20Is against India, including figures of 3/24 in Ranchi and 2/38 in Indore. With the bat, Chase has merely got a chance to bat and has only managed to score 10 runs in two innings, including an unbeaten five in the third T20I."I understand why I get a lot of criticism for having Roston in the team, but I understand the individual he is," Sammy said."Roston is naturally very disciplined in all aspects of his life. He does not like conceding runs, so he has a very clear defensive mindset." Sammy said Chase understood how to avoid being hit and had a clear idea of his bowling plans, adding that his intelligence and ability to execute those plans made him an important member of the line-up."He knows how not to get hit, and he is an intelligent cricketer," he said.Sammy also dismissed the perception that West Indies' batting depended heavily on Shai Hope, who has been in strong form. He praised the calmness Hope brings to the middle but said other batters had also made important contributions.He pointed to Brandon King's batting alongside Hope in the ODIs and cited knocks from Shimron Hetmyer and Sherfane Rutherford as examples of the team's depth."He brings calm to the middle when he is there, and perhaps some of our other players need to adapt to that calmness when the pressure is on. But he is not the only reason we win games," Sammy said.Sammy also praised the leadership qualities of a player who continued to guide and challenge teammates despite struggling for runs. Recalling the dressing room after West Indies' 2-1 T20I series win over Sri Lanka in 2026, Sammy said the player had never lost his voice as a leader despite his own shortcomings."He was still able to challenge his teammates even when his own performances were limited, and I admire that quality in him," Sammy said.

title: India need attacking mindset to take wickets vs West Indies, says Tilak
summary: India are 2-1 ahead in the series, and a win on Wednesday will give them an unassailable lead, while the visitors will be eager to draw level
fullText: India need to hunt for wickets rather than containing a power-packed West Indies batting line-up, vice-captain Tilak Varma said on Tuesday, stressing the importance of bowling plan execution as the hosts look to seal the five-match T20 International series in the fourth game itself.India are 2-1 ahead in the series and a win on Wednesday will give them an unassailable lead, while the visitors will be eager to draw level.The West Indies demonstrated their batting firepower by chasing down India's 249 in the second T20I, with skipper Shai Hope smashing a 45-ball 102.Tilak said India ill afford to relax against a side whose power-hitting extends till the last batter in the line-up."The West Indies are a really good side, especially in T20 format. They play so much franchise cricket, so they know how to play this format. The power they have is unbelievable," Tilak said at the pre-match press conference on Tuesday."Everyone can hit the ball. It is not just the openers, number three or four. All their players can strike the ball, and even the 11th batter can come in and hit. Until all 10 wickets fall, the game is not over. We cannot relax." India's bowling unit came under scrutiny after the second match defeat. The visitors capitalised in the powerplay to pull off a remarkable chase.The 23-year-old Tilak said the team had reviewed its defensive approach in that match, with head coach Gautam Gambhir encouraging the bowlers to be more aggressive and to attack for wickets instead of allowing the opposition to dictate terms."Initially, in the second game, we did not go for wickets. We were slightly defensive when they (West Indies) were scoring runs. But after that, as a team, Gautam (Gambhir) sir also mentioned that we can go for wickets and show that aggression," he said.India bounced back with a 14-run win in the third T20I in Indore, restricting the West Indies to 209 despite another late assault from the visitors.Tilak said the team would look to build on that performance, with a better execution of plans against an opposition capable of changing the course of a match within a few overs.With India's top batters in good form, the middle order has had limited opportunities. Tilak, who has scored 443 runs in 13 T20I innings at number three with the help of two centuries at an average of 55.37 and a strike rate of 169.73, said he was ready to adapt to the team's requirements."I love batting at number three, and I have said that many times. I always want that pressure. When the team needs me, I want to step up," he said."If quick wickets fall, I can take my time and take the game deep. But if the openers or the top three batters have batted until the 14th or 15th over, I know how to change the gears from the first ball." The re-laid pitch at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium is expected to offer a different challenge from the venue's usual surface. Tilak said India would assess the conditions before deciding on their approach with the bat."You cannot go all out from the first ball without assessing the conditions. In one-day cricket, you can take five or six balls to understand the wicket, but in T20 cricket, you have only one or two balls before you need to get going," he said."Haven't seen the track yet but will see how the conditions behave initially and go accordingly. It is a fresh soil track, so let's see how it goes." Tilak also explained his run-out in the previous match after he and Axar Patel mistakenly thought that a shot towards deep backward square leg had reached the boundary.The confusion followed Axar's flick towards the leg-side boundary, with the West Indies fielder diving to stop the ball. Tilak thought the ball had crossed the rope and began walking away from his crease, while Axar initially shared the same impression.The ball, however, remained in play, and the West Indies fielders threw it back to complete the run-out at the bowler's end as Axar returned safely to his crease."Both Axar and I felt the same way. We thought it was a boundary, which is why I was walking. Unfortunately, the ball was thrown to Axar's end, and he was shown the ball," Tilak said."I did not see the ball. I thought it had gone for four, so I was walking. But these things happen in cricket." The fourth T20I will also be a special occasion for Tilak, who is set to play in front of his home crowd. He said he was looking forward to the experience, with several Sunrisers Hyderabad players, including Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Nitish Kumar Reddy, also part of the Indian squad."It is really a proud moment for me to play in front of Hyderabad crowd as vice-captain of the Indian team. It will be a special moment for me," he said.

title: ACT to be final India assignment for four senior hockey players: Reports
summary: Hockey India sources confirmed to PTI that these four players will make their last India appearances at the ACT to be held from October 27 to November 5
fullText: Four senior India hockey players -- Mandeep Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Amit Rohidas and Nilakanta Sharma -- are set to play their last matches for the country during the upcoming Asian Champions Trophy to be held in Jalandhar and Mohali, according to sources.Hockey India sources confirmed to PTI that these four players will make their last India appearances at the ACT to be held from October 27 to November 5 as fresh legs are needed in the team, keeping in mind the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics."Yes, it has been in discussion for sometime among the selectors because we need to bring in and groom young players for the LA Olympics. These four players have served the country for a long time but now it's time for fresh legs. We are thankful to their services," a Hockey India source told PTI on conditions of anonymity.Striker Mandeep, 31, has played 301 matches for India, scoring 128 goals with 11 hat-tricks as per the statistics of the International Hockey Federation (FIH).An Arjuna awardee, Mandeep has two Olympic bronze medals, two gold and a bronze in Asian Games, besides numerous accolades to his name.The 30-year-old Jarmanpreet has been a rock in the Indian defence, and has earned 171 India caps, scoring eight goals. He was part of the 2024 Paris Olympics bronze-winning squad and gold-winning teams of 2022 and 2026 Asian Games. He was also a part of the 2018 Champions Trophy silver medal-winning squad.Rohidas, 33, has 257 caps to his name and he has scored 38 goals. One the first rushers of the Indian team while defending penalty corners, Rohidas has won back-to-back Olympic bronze medals in Tokyo and Paris, Champions Trophy silver in 2018, back-to-back Asian Games gold in 2022 and 2026. He was also a part of the bronze-winning team in the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta.The 31-year-old Nilakanta, who has 162 caps and 19 goals to his name, is the other player who is set to play his farewell tournament during the ACT.Nilakanta, a midfielder from Manipur, was part of India's bronze medal-winning squad at the Tokyo Olympics, and gold winning teams of 2022 and 2026 Asian Games.The decision has been taken to make a smooth transition in the team to prepare for the 2028 Olympics, HI sources said.

title: Hazlewood shines as Australia beat South Africa by 214 runs in Durban Test
summary: A target of 421 was always improbable for South Africa and the world champion Proteas were cleaned up less than an hour after lunch and within five overs of Australia taking the second new ball
fullText: Josh Hazlewood's career-best 6-49 helped Australia win the first cricket test by 214 runs at Kingsmead and finish off South Africa on the final day Tuesday.Hazlewood took four of the six wickets Australia was hunting for on day five.A target of 421 was always improbable for South Africa and the world champion Proteas were cleaned up less than an hour after lunch and within five overs of Australia taking the second new ball.South Africa was all out for 206 after 284 in the first innings.Middle-order batter Matt Renshaw was easily the standout player with 190 runs in Australia's first innings of 390 and 82 in the second total of 314-6 declared. Renshaw's part-time spin also netted the first two wickets of his test career.Opening batter Aiden Markram led South Africa's fourth-innings resistance for nearly six hours with a 237-ball knock for 75 before he was ninth man out. Markram was caught behind off an inside edge to Mitchell Starc. He was initially given not out but Australia reviewed.Hazlewood broke the defiant stand between Markram and Wiaan Mulder that started late Monday and endured for nearly two more hours on Tuesday.The end of Mulder's 110-ball innings for 29, after resuming on 5, brought in Kyle Verreynne, who was dismissed on 1 three balls later.Renshaw also began a second stint and Verreynne tried to cut him but gave Steve Smith a slips catch and Renshaw his second wicket of the innings, and of his career.Smith did not take the field on Monday evening after he was hit on the helmet while batting and underwent a concussion test. He came out to field on day five after medical reports cleared him.Markram and Marco Jansen safely reached lunch after a morning session in which South Africa scored only 64 runs in 32 overs, banking on survival against an Australia attack that was squeezing the Proteas on a fifth-day pitch that did not break up as expected.South Africa hopes were pinned on Markram, who has a history of thwarting the Australians in the fourth innings. He defied them for 143 in another lost cause in Durban in 2018 but scored 136 to overcome Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord's. This was the first test between the teams since then.Markram in the morning became only the second batter in the match after Renshaw to score a half-century and had 69 by lunch.But he lost partners rapidly after Australia took the new ball in the 82nd over.Jansen was beaten through the gate by a Hazlewood nip-backer on 35, and Simon Harmer went in the same over to a riser that brushed his glove and shoulder and that Carey had to leap high for. That gave Hazlewood his 15th test five-for.Markram went in the next over and the match finished in the over after that when Hazlewood claimed his sixth wicket of the innings.Renshaw had 2-30 and Starc and Pat Cummins a wicket each.The second of three tests starts on Sunday at Gqeberha.

title: UCL 2026: Barcelona, Arsenal secure easy wins; Man United goes down 0-2
summary: Barcelona's 100 per cent start to the season was under threat down 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul, but the Spanish champion rallied to a 4-1 win
fullText: Barcelona survived a scare against Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday. But Bayern Munich was stunned by a late equaliser from Viking in a 3-3 draw in Norway.Arsenal rolled over Lille and it was more misery for Manchester United.Barcelona's 100 per cent start to the season was under threat down 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul, but the Spanish champion rallied to a 4-1 win.Bayern was in even more trouble against Viking, trailing 2-0 at halftime before Harry Kane turned the game around with two goals after the break. Luis Diaz looked to have completed the comeback, but a red card for Michael Olise and a 90th minute goal from Herman Haugen provided another twist.Arsenal cruised to a 3-0 win at home over Lille and Atletico Madrid piled more pressure on United coach Michael Carrick with a 2-0 win at the Metropolitano.Inter Milan fell to a surprise 4-3 home loss to Club Brugge, and Villarreal beat Napoli 3-1.10 out of 10 for Barcelona It's 10 straight wins for Barcelona after it maintained its perfect record in all competitions despite early trouble in Turkey.Aleksey Batrakov gave Galatasaray the lead before his team had a second goal ruled out for a tight offside. Joao Cancelo's goal leveled the score just before halftime and it was all Barcelona after that with goals from Fermin Lopez, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi."In the second half, we dominated the game," Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said."We have to play like this, control the game, move the ball. This is our quality. This is our strength, and we have to show our level." Late drama for Bayern A bizarre sending-off for Olise paved the way for Norwegian team Viking to rescue a draw in its first Champions League home game since 1992.Shortly after Bayern went ahead 3-2, Olise picked up two yellow cards in quick succession - the second for tossing the ball at opponent Zlatko Tripic while the referee was still booking him for his first foul.Tripic then provided the cross that allowed Haugen to head in the equalizer in the 90th minute."We were dominant, but at the moment it feels like every chance for the opposition leads to a goal," Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said.Martinez lashes out Lisandro Martinez hit out at Manchester United's hierarchy after the club extended its winless run to five games.Michael Carrick's team has won just two games in all competitions this term and fell to a fourth loss after goals from Pablo Barrios in the first minute and Ademola Lookman in the second half.Speaking afterward, Martinez was critical of United's off-season recruitment."I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection in the mirror of how is our club at the moment," the Argentina defender told Amazon Prime."We did a fantastic season last season. And now we expect more from the top, from up, to bring more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well, and today also Atletico they have an amazing team and they deserved to win today."I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it's just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night." In London, Bukayo Saka stepped off the bench to score a goal in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Lille.The England forward came on after 65 minutes at the Emirates and within two minutes set up at goal for Eberechi Eze. Four minutes later he was on the score sheet himself.Jurrien Timber had given Arsenal the lead in the 64th.Tresoldi's reputation grows Nicolo Tresoldi is emerging as one of the brightest prospects in Europe and he enhanced his reputation with a hat trick in Brugge's seven-goal thriller against Inter.The Italian-born Germany under-21 international opened the scoring with a first-half penalty and completed his hat trick with two more after the break.Lautaro Martinez scored twice for Inter."It was my dream as a kid to play here," he told broadcaster Proximus Belgium."I was here in the stands as a kid watching Milan and tonight I played against Inter. It can't get any better. I was shaking before the penalty, but it was the perfect moment." There was also defeat for Napoli at Villarreal despite going ahead early on through Amir Rrahmani.Historic win for Sabah Azerbaijani outsider Sabah claimed its first win in the league phase of the competition by beating Slavia Prague 2-0.Second-half goals from Kaheem Parris and Joy-Lance Mickels secured the historic win in Baku. The club was only founded nine years ago.Sporting Lisbon also sealed a 2-0 win at Lens through goals from Luis Suarez and Issa Doumbia.Brajan Gruda's first Champions League goal lifted Leipzig to a 1-0 win over PSV Eindhoven to rebound after a heavy opening loss to newcomer Como. Leipzig keeper Maarten Vandevoordt earlier saved a penalty from PSV's Ivan Perisic.

title: Lisandro Martinez slams Man United hierarchy after Champions League loss
summary: In a post-game interview on Tuesday, Martinez questioned the club's off-season recruitment after it had secured a return to the Champions League this season
fullText: Lisandro Martinez added to Manchester United's troubled start to the season by calling out the club's hierarchy following a 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.In a post-game interview on Tuesday, Martinez questioned the club's off-season recruitment after it had secured a return to the Champions League this season."I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection in the mirror of how is our club at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime."We did a fantastic season last season. And now we expect more from the top, from up, to bring more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well, and today also Atletico they have an amazing team and they deserved to win today."I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it's just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night." Jason Wilcox is United's director of football and the club spent around USD 213 million on players like Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in the off-season. But it has endured a difficult start to the campaign.Defeat in Madrid extended United's winless run to five games in all competitions. It has won only once in the Premier League and is 13th in the standings."Last season we did everything, we create the base to be an amazing team," Martinez said."It's annoying, disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here, it's disappointing." Pablo Barrios scored in the first minute for Atletico and Ademola Lookman sealed victory in the second half.The latest setback will add to the pressure on United coach Michael Carrick."You start changing, changing, changing manager. But what about other areas?" Martinez said."I can't say more.

title: IPL 2027: DC rope in Yuvraj Singh as new assistant and batting coach
summary: A veteran of 304 ODIs, 40 Tests, and 58 T20Is, as well as a multiple World Cup winner, the 44-year-old has also mentored several established and emerging Indian stars in recent years
fullText: The JSW and GMR co-owned Delhi Capitals announced the appointment of former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh as Assistant & Batting Coach of the franchise on Tuesday ahead of the upcoming season of the Indian Premier League.A veteran of 304 ODIs, 40 Tests, and 58 T20Is, as well as a multiple World Cup winner, the 44-year-old has also mentored several established and emerging Indian stars in recent years. This appointment marks his first formal coaching role, with Yuvraj set to make his IPL coaching debut with Delhi Capitals, according to a press release from DC.The appointment also marks a reunion with the Delhi franchise for Yuvraj. In 2015, the franchise (then Delhi Daredevils) secured his services for a record Rs 16 crore, which made him the most expensive player in IPL history at the time. He went on to represent the franchise in all 14 matches that season.Speaking on the appointment, Delhi Capitals Chairman and Co-owner and JSW Sports Founder, Parth Jindal, said, as per the release, "We are absolutely thrilled to welcome Yuvi to the Delhi Capitals family. Yuvi is one of Indian cricket's greatest match-winners and someone who has played a pivotal role in mentoring many of the brightest young talents in Indian cricket today. His experience, winning mindset, and ability to connect with players will be invaluable to our squad.""We wish him all the very best as he takes on his first formal coaching role, and we are excited to begin this new chapter together. His return to the franchise also marks a special moment for everyone associated with the Capitals, and we look forward to seeing him work with Dada and the rest of the staff going forward," he added.Kiran Kumar Grandhi, Co-owner, Delhi Capitals, and GMR Sports Founder, said, "We are delighted to welcome Yuvraj Singh to Delhi Capitals as our Assistant & Batting Coach. His remarkable career, competitive spirit and deep understanding of the game make him a tremendous addition to our coaching setup."This marks his first formal coaching role in the IPL, and we are confident that his insights, winning mindset and ability to mentor players will make a meaningful difference to our players and our campaign. We look forward to working closely with him and wish him every success as he begins this exciting new chapter with Delhi Capitals," he added.Speaking on his new role, Yuvraj said, "I am excited to begin a new chapter in my life with the Delhi Capitals. I have an old association with the franchise and know the owners well, which makes this a special opportunity for me. I'm also looking forward to teaming up with Dada, this time as coaches. Coaching is something I am truly passionate about, and I cannot wait to get started with this extremely talented squad. I'm sure it's going to be an exciting journey for me, and I look forward to contributing to the team's success."One of India's key architects of the country's triumphs in the 2007 ICC T20 World Cup and the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup, Yuvraj enjoyed a distinguished IPL career, featuring in 132 matches, scoring 2,750 runs, and taking 36 wickets.
