title: FIFA plans to double development funding; India could receive $25 million
summary: The plan also includes $99 million for each of FIFA's six continental confederations over the same period
fullText: FIFA is expected to propose more than $6 billion in football development funding for the 2027-30 cycle, more than double the amount previously earmarked for the four-year period. Under the proposal, each member association, including the All India Football Federation (AIFF), could receive $25 million, compared with the previously planned $10 million. The plan also includes $99 million for each of FIFA's six continental confederations over the same period. To finance the increase, the governing body would distribute more than $3.5 billion from its financial reserves while retaining cash reserves of $1.7 billion. The proposal is set to be discussed by the FIFA Council on Thursday, October 15, before a consultation process and potential finalisation in December. It would then require approval at the FIFA Congress in March 2027. The proposed increase follows the commercial success of the 2026 FIFA World Cup and comes amid scrutiny of President Gianni Infantino following the abandonment of a private investment initiative.AIFF's FIFA funding: Current system vs proposed $25 million allocationUnder FIFA's existing Forward 3.0 programme for 2023-26, each member association is eligible for up to $8 million over four years. This includes up to $1.25 million annually for operational costs, $3 million for approved development projects and, for eligible associations with annual revenue not exceeding $4 million, up to $1 million for travel and accommodation over the cycle. For the 2027-30 cycle, the earlier plan was to increase the allocation to $10 million per member association. The latest proposal would raise that figure to $25 million, an increase of $15 million over four years. If approved, AIFF would fall within the scope of the proposed allocation as one of FIFA's 211 member associations. However, the proposed $25 million should not be treated as a confirmed cash payment. The final programme rules will determine the applicable conditions and disbursement arrangements. FIFA's published India development figures list approximately $2.70 million in committed infrastructure funding and $4.34 million for competitions. These are project-funding figures and do not represent AIFF's total receipts from FIFA.FIFA plans to use more than $3.5 billion from reservesFIFA would distribute more than $3.5 billion from its financial reserves to support the proposed increase, according to a source briefed on the plans. The source spoke anonymously because they were not authorised to discuss the proposal publicly. The plan would allow FIFA to retain cash reserves of $1.7 billion while increasing funding available to member associations and confederations during the four-year cycle. Each member association would receive a proposed $25 million, while each of the six confederations would be allocated $99 million over the same period. If approved, the proposal would continue the expansion of FIFA's development funding under President Gianni Infantino, who took charge of the governing body in 2016. According to the report, the amount allocated to each member association would have risen from $1 million to $25 million during his presidency. ALSO READ: IPL 2027: Here's why BCCI postponed the October 15 stakeholders' meeting2026 World Cup revenue exceeds FIFA's projectionsThe proposed increase follows the commercial success of the 2026 men's FIFA World Cup, jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. FIFA generated approximately $15 billion from the tournament, exceeding its original revenue projection of $11 billion. The governing body subsequently revised that estimate to $13 billion. The expanded 48-team format contributed to the tournament's unprecedented commercial scale, providing the financial backdrop for FIFA's proposal to increase the resources available for football development. The funding plan is expected to be discussed by the FIFA Council, the governing body's main decision-making body, on Thursday, October 15. If approved to proceed, it will undergo consultation before potentially being finalised by the Council in December. The proposal would then require final approval at the FIFA Congress in March 2027.Funding proposal follows FIFA Forward Enterprise controversyThe planned increase in distributions comes after FIFA abandoned its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative, which would have made a 20 per cent stake in the governing body's commercial and event operations available for private investment. The proposal triggered criticism from senior football officials and placed Infantino under scrutiny. Aleksander Ceferin, president of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), and Victor Montagliani, president of the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (Concacaf), both called on Infantino to resign following the controversy. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), also previously supported calls for Infantino to stand down. However, he has since appeared to soften his position and reversed his earlier call for an independent body to review FIFA's governance. Ceferin and Montagliani have also written to Infantino seeking the release of a portion of FIFA's reserves for distribution to member associations. Thursday's Council meeting will be the first since the FFE proposal was abandoned, bringing the proposed funding increase into focus alongside the governance controversy.Infantino faces re-election next yearThe funding proposal comes as Infantino prepares to seek another term as FIFA president in 2027. Despite calling for his resignation, neither Ceferin nor Montagliani has entered the presidential race or put forward an alternative candidate. Both have remained in their respective confederation roles. Infantino is currently expected to run unopposed for the third consecutive time unless another candidate enters the race before the November 18 deadline. The proposed funding increase would expand the resources available to FIFA's member associations, including AIFF, but remains subject to approval by the governing body's decision-making bodies.

title: IPL 2027: Here's why BCCI postponed the October 15 stakeholders' meeting

title: Virat Kohli makes Linkedin debut after choosing equity over endorsement
summary: Kohli reportedly turned down a renewal offer worth Rs 300 crore over eight years from Puma, choosing an equity-based partnership with Agilitas Sports instead
fullText: Star Indian batter and former captain Virat Kohli made his debut on professional networking platform LinkedIn on Tuesday, sharing his vision for India's sports industry and his decision to invest in Agilitas Sports after ending his association with Puma. The 37-year-old has invested Rs 40 crore in the Bengaluru-based sportswear company for a 1.94 per cent equity stake and joined as an investor, while becoming a co-founder and co-creator of one8world. Kohli reportedly turned down a renewal offer worth Rs 300 crore over eight years from Puma, choosing an equity-based partnership instead. Agilitas has acquired one8world as part of the arrangement, with plans to develop it into a global sportswear brand. The company, founded by former Puma executive Abhishek Ganguly, is building capabilities across manufacturing, product development, distribution and retail.What Kohli said in his first LinkedIn postKohli said he had always wanted to see an India where every sport was followed, celebrated and played. He added that a new generation was demonstrating the country's ability to produce world-class athletes and build brands for international markets. Explaining his association with Agilitas, Kohli said the company's vision was to build an end-to-end sports platform from India, spanning manufacturing, consumer brands and sports distribution. He described one8 as a brand built on pushing boundaries, raising standards and doing things differently. Recalling its launch in his home city, he said the occasion was among the most meaningful moments of his life. Kohli added that the objective was to build something that would outlast the people involved in the venture. ALSO READ: India's poor Asiad medal haul sparks scrutiny of sports funding for LA 2028Virat Kohli's Rs 40 crore investment in Agilitas SportsAccording to regulatory filings cited in media reports, Kohli invested Rs 40 crore in Agilitas through compulsorily convertible preference shares, securing a 1.94 per cent equity stake in the company. Agilitas has been valued at approximately Rs 2,058 crore following its funding activity, according to reports. The transaction marks a shift from Kohli's earlier endorsement-based arrangement with Puma towards equity ownership in a sportswear business. His investment gives him a stake in Agilitas beyond his role in developing one8world. Kohli's reported decision to reject a Rs 300 crore Puma contract extension over eight years preceded the move. His original association with Puma began in 2017, when one8 was developed through a licensing collaboration with the German sportswear company.How Agilitas plans to expand one8worldFounded in 2023 by Abhishek Ganguly, former managing director of Puma India and Southeast Asia, along with Atul Bajaj and Amit Prabhu, Agilitas is building a business covering sportswear manufacturing, research and development, brand development and retail distribution. The company acquired footwear manufacturer Mochiko Shoes in 2023, strengthening its manufacturing capabilities. It also secured licensing rights for Italian sportswear brand Lotto in India. Under the new arrangement, one8world will operate as an independent sports brand within Agilitas' wider business platform. Kohli will contribute to product development, including performance, functionality, design and finish, while the company works towards expanding the brand into international markets.Who else has invested in Agilitas Sports?Kohli is among several prominent names associated with Agilitas. Other investors include actor Anushka Sharma, former India cricketer Yuvraj Singh, singer Hardy Sandhu and Indian batter Abhishek Sharma. Yuvraj Singh reportedly holds a 0.51 per cent stake in the company. Agilitas has also received institutional backing from investors, including Nexus Venture Partners and Convergent Finance-advised funds. The company's strategy combines manufacturing capabilities with sportswear brands and distribution, with the stated ambition of building Indian brands that can compete in international markets.LinkedIn welcomes Kohli to its professional networkKumaresh Pattabiraman, country manager of LinkedIn India, welcomed Kohli to the platform, saying his entrepreneurial journey could inspire professionals building businesses and pursuing opportunities beyond a single career. Pattabiraman said LinkedIn had 185 million members in India and more than one billion professionals worldwide who use the platform to connect, learn and grow their businesses. Kohli's first post sets out his ambitions in sportswear and his role in Agilitas, alongside his continuing career in cricket.

title: India's poor Asiad medal haul sparks scrutiny of sports funding for LA 2028
summary: India finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Games with 85 medals, comprising 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, compared with 106 medals at Hangzhou in 2022
fullText: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is set to review the performance of National Sports Federations (NSFs) following India's underwhelming campaign at the 2026 Asian Games, with the outcome potentially influencing preparations and funding priorities for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. The meeting, originally scheduled for October 13, has been postponed to October 15. According to an NDTV report, at least nine federations could face questions over their medal returns, particularly in sports that received government support but failed to meet expectations. India finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Games with 85 medals, comprising 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, compared with 106 medals at Hangzhou in 2022. The review is expected to examine the performance of experienced athletes, the effectiveness of government assistance and the planning of federations. However, no decision on plans to cut funding has been announced yet.Asian Games medal tally puts federations under scrutinyIndia's 85-medal finish was its second-highest tally at the Asian Games, but the 21-medal decline from Hangzhou has prompted questions about results in sports where the country had established medal prospects. The Indian Olympic Association confirmed that India finished fourth, with athletics contributing 24 medals, shooting 15 and archery nine. The Ministry's review is expected to focus on experienced athletes who failed to reach the podium, including competitors supported through the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). The scheme provides financial assistance to athletes identified as potential medal winners at major international competitions. A ministry source told NDTV that at least nine federations would face questions during the review. The source also raised concerns about the returns from government expenditure and said the performance of athletes who withdrew because of injuries would be examined. The ministry personnel said 89 experienced athletes supported through TOPS failed to win medals across 23 disciplines. More than ₹27 crore had been spent on 34 elite athletes across nine disciplines who did not secure a medal at the Games. These figures have become part of the discussion about whether athlete support, preparation and selection decisions are producing the intended results. However, India's overall tally also included significant achievements. Archery won five gold medals, while boxing and wrestling secured three and two gold medals, respectively. The men's and women's cricket teams won their respective titles, as did the men's and women's hockey teams and the kabaddi teams. ALSO READ: ECB expands England central contracts from 30 to 39 for 2026-27 cycleContingent size and medal returns raise questionsThe sport-wise figures show considerable variation in India's medal returns. Athletics sent 75 athletes and won 24 medals, while shooting's 30-member contingent won 15. Archery sent 12 athletes and secured nine medals. Badminton, by contrast, sent 20 athletes and won one bronze, while fencing's 20-member contingent returned without a medal. Rowing sent 22 athletes and won one bronze. Canoeing, cycling, equestrian, esports, swimming and several other disciplines did not contribute to the medal tally. The figures offer a starting point for assessing performance, but contingent size should not be treated as a direct measure of success. Sports differ in the number of medal events and the strength of their competitive fields. Injuries, withdrawals, selection decisions and preparation also affect outcomes. India's sport-wise contingent size and medal tally at the 2026 Asian Games SportContingent sizeTotal medalsMedals (G-S-B)Archery1295-2-2Shooting30153-8-4Boxing1163-0-3Wrestling1562-2-2Cricket2922-0-0Field hockey4022-0-0Kabaddi2422-0-0Athletics75241-9-14Golf621-1-0Squash850-2-3Sailing1030-1-2Weightlifting410-1-0Wushu710-1-0Badminton2010-0-1Kurash610-0-1Mixed martial arts210-0-1Rowing2210-0-1Sepak takraw2110-0-1Soft tennis610-0-1Table tennis1010-0-1Canoeing1900-0-0Cycling1400-0-0Equestrian700-0-0Esports1500-0-0Fencing2000-0-0Gymnastics100-0-0Judo300-0-0Karate200-0-0Rugby sevens1300-0-0Sport climbing200-0-0Surfing400-0-0Swimming1200-0-0Taekwondo300-0-0Tennis700-0-0Teqball300-0-0Volleyball1200-0-0TOTAL4958521-27-37Badminton's Asian Games return draws attentionBadminton is among the sports expected to face questions after India's 20-member contingent returned from Aichi-Nagoya with one bronze medal, won by the men's team. The individual campaign did not produce another podium finish. The defending men's doubles champions, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, were knocked out in the opening round, while P V Sindhu also exited early. The results contrasted with India's previous achievements in international badminton and have raised questions about preparation and performance at a major multi-sport event. Accommodation arrangements have also attracted attention. The contingent stayed at the five-star Nagoya Tokyu hotel, where rooms were reported to cost approximately ₹13,729 per night. Other athletes were accommodated in hotels, temporary facilities and the cruise ship Costa Serena. The issue is whether the support provided translated into the expected competitive results. Accommodation costs alone, however, cannot establish whether resources were used effectively or whether they affected performance. Transport difficulties in reaching the badminton venue in Ichinomiya and scheduling concerns involving Sindhu were also reported. She played three matches within 24 hours, according to the account of the Games. Such logistical problems are relevant when assessing the campaign, although they do not by themselves explain the results. Before the Games, Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav said the Ministry had instructed officials to ensure athletes received the facilities they needed. He said: “The Ministry has told us to spend as much as we need to see that athletes have every comfort.” The review will need to distinguish between performance issues within a federation's control and difficulties arising from event scheduling or transport arrangements. Preparation, coaching, competition exposure, selection decisions and athlete fitness will also be relevant to an assessment of the badminton campaign.LA 2028 funding review puts future plans in focusThe Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports spent ₹800.70 crore on India's preparations for the 2026 Asian Games during the 2023–2026 cycle, comprising ₹702.86 crore under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competitions (ACTC) and ₹97.84 crore under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). The spending has come under scrutiny following India's 85-medal finish at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, down from 106 medals at Hangzhou in 2022. The Ministry's review is expected to examine whether the support provided to athletes and federations is translating into the expected competitive results. A report by The Indian Express said ₹27.16 crore was spent on 34 elite athletes across nine sports who did not win medals at the Asian Games. The expenditure has become part of the debate around TOPS, although spending on athletes who failed to win medals does not, by itself, establish that the scheme has been ineffective. TOPS provides targeted assistance to athletes identified as potential medal winners at major international competitions. Support can cover customised training programmes, overseas exposure, coaching, specialised equipment and sports science services. The scheme also provides monthly stipends to eligible athletes under its core and developmental categories.How India performed at the 2024 Paris OlympicsIndia won six medals at the Paris Olympics in 2024, comprising one silver and five bronze, and finished 71st in the medal standings. The tally was one medal fewer than the seven India won at the Tokyo Olympics in 2020. India also recorded six fourth-place finishes in Paris. Neeraj Chopra won India's only silver medal in the men's javelin throw, finishing behind Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem. Shooting contributed three bronze medals, making it India's most successful sport at the Games. Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10m air pistol and then partnered Sarabjot Singh to secure another bronze in the mixed 10m air pistol team event. Swapnil Kusale won the third shooting medal in the men's 50m rifle three positions. The men's hockey team won bronze after defeating Spain 2-1, while wrestler Aman Sehrawat secured bronze in the men's freestyle 57kg category. India's Paris campaign was notable for its six-medal return, but the absence of a gold medal and the number of fourth-place finishes also drew attention to the narrow margins separating podium finishes from near misses.

title: ECB expands England central contracts from 30 to 39 for 2026-27 cycle
summary: Uncapped Crocombe's two-year contract marks the first time an England men's player has received a multi-year central deal before making his international debut
fullText: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) announced its new central contract list on Monday, expanding the number of centrally contracted players from 30 to 39 for the 2026-27 cycle, awarding 30 full central contracts and nine development deals. The list includes seven players receiving new full contracts, while the retirements of Ben Stokes and Mark Wood have freed up funds for the revised structure. Uncapped seamer Henry Crocombe and batter Jordan Cox have been handed two-year deals, while former Test opener Zak Crawley and left-arm seamer Luke Wood have lost their full contracts.Seven players earn new full central contractsTom Banton, Sam Cook, Emilio Gay, Matthew Fisher, Dan Lawrence and Ollie Robinson have received one-year contracts after impressing England's management this summer. Crocombe and Cox are the two players to sign new two-year deals. Crocombe's contract marks the first time an England men's player has received a multi-year central deal before making his international debut. The seamer took 40 wickets at an average of 23.52 in Division One of the County Championship this season, including two hat-tricks. He has previously been named in England's Test and ODI squads. Crocombe said at the Toyota PCA Awards this month that he wanted to improve his white-ball cricket to make himself available for England across all formats.Nine players secure deals until September 2028Nine players who were already centrally contracted have extended their agreements until September 2028. The group comprises Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook, Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Joe Root and Josh Tongue. Meanwhile, Jos Buttler, Brydon Carse, Ben Duckett, Adil Rashid and Jamie Smith are entering the second year of their existing two-year contracts. Their deals run until the end of England's 2027 home summer, which includes an Ashes series, a one-off Test against Bangladesh and white-ball series against Pakistan and New Zealand. Seven other players have had their contracts renewed until September 2027: Rehan Ahmed, Liam Dawson, Saqib Mahmood, Jamie Overton, Ollie Pope, Matthew Potts and Phil Salt. Shoaib Bashir has also received a one-year extension after playing only two Tests during the previous contract year. ALSO READ: WPL 2027: Mumbai Indians complete first-ever trade to sign Tara NorrisStokes, Wood retirements free up fundsStokes and Mark Wood have retired from international cricket, while Crawley and Luke Wood are the other players from last season's full central contract list who have not been retained. Tom Lawes has also dropped off the development contract list. The ECB's agreement with the Team England Player Partnership requires the board to spend the fixed amount allocated for central contracts each year. England managing director Rob Key said the departure of high-earning players had created additional room to distribute funds differently. "When you lose a few big-name players, that releases more money to be able to use in different ways," Key said. Key also defended the ECB's decision to offer multi-year deals to players who have yet to establish themselves fully at international level, saying the structure allows England to make longer-term commitments and plan players' development over two years. The multi-year contract system was introduced in 2023 partly to address the threat posed by franchise cricket, with the ECB seeking to reduce the risk of players turning down international opportunities in favour of year-round T20 leagues.Nine players receive development contractsThe ECB has awarded development contracts to James Coles, Mason Crane, Josh Hull, Eddie Jack, Ben McKinney, Liam Patterson-White, Thomas Rew, Matthew Revis and Mitchell Stanley. Under the arrangement, the ECB covers half of a player's existing county salary and provides an additional 25 per cent top-up. The deals are intended to strengthen the England Lions programme by giving the board greater flexibility to select players for representative cricket, even when they have county or franchise commitments. Key said the ECB expected players on development contracts to make themselves available for Lions cricket when selected.Carse remains under investigationBrydon Carse remains subject to an investigation by the Cricket Regulator after he was briefly arrested outside a nightclub in Derby this summer. He has not been selected for England in any format since the incident. Key said he did not currently see anything to suggest Carse would lose his contract, but added that the ECB would assess the situation as the investigation progressed. England's white-ball squad is due to travel to Pakistan for an ODI tri-series involving Sri Lanka before heading to Australia in November for three ODIs and five T20Is. The ECB is scheduled to announce the squad for the Australia tour on Tuesday.England’s updated central contracts:Two-year contracts: Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Joe Root, Josh Tongue (to 30 September 2028) One-year contracts: Rehan Ahmed, Tom Banton, Shoaib Bashir, Jos Buttler, Brydon Carse, Sam Cook, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Matthew Fisher, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Saqib Mahmood, Jamie Overton, Ollie Pope, Matthew Potts, Adil Rashid, Ollie Robinson, Phil Salt, Jamie Smith (to 30 September 2027) Development contracts: James Coles, Mason Crane, Josh Hull, Eddie Jack, Ben McKinney, Liam Patterson-White, Thomas Rew, Matthew Revis, Mitchell Stanley (to 30 September 2027) Removed from contract: Zak Crawley, Ben Stokes (retired), Luke Wood, Mark Wood (retired).

title: WPL 2027: Mumbai Indians complete first-ever trade to sign Tara Norris
summary: Norris's arrival also gives MI the option of fielding five overseas players in their playing XI, as players from Associate nations are exempt from the usual four overseas-player limit
fullText: Mumbai Indians (MI) have completed their first-ever player trade in the Women’s Premier League (WPL) history, as they rope in United States left-arm seamer Tara Norris from UP Warriorz (UPW) at her existing fee of Rs 10 lakh ahead of the 2027 season. The 28-year-old becomes part of the two-time champions’ squad after previously representing Delhi Capitals in the inaugural WPL season in 2023. Norris made history during that campaign by becoming the first bowler to take a five-wicket haul in the competition. Norris’s arrival also gives MI the option of fielding five overseas players in their playing XI, as players from Associate nations are exempt from the usual four overseas-player limit.Tara Norris joins Mumbai Indians at existing feeThe WPL confirmed that Norris would move to Mumbai Indians for the same Rs 10 lakh fee at which UP Warriorz had signed her ahead of the 2026 season. The left-arm seamer was previously part of the Delhi Capitals squad during the inaugural WPL season. She became the first player from an Associate nation to be picked at the WPL auction before making her mark on the field in 2023. Norris has represented the United States in five women’s one-day internationals (WODIs) and 17 women’s T20 internationals (WT20Is). She made her international debut for the USA in 2021. ALSO READ: Ranji Trophy: Here's why Arunachal Pradesh forfeited their game vs NagalandNorris’ WPL recordNorris announced herself in the inaugural WPL season with a five-wicket haul against Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the Brabourne Stadium. She returned figures of 5 for 29, dismissing Ellyse Perry, Heather Knight and Richa Ghosh, among others. UP Warriorz signed Norris ahead of the 2025 season, but she subsequently withdrew to represent the USA in the Women’s T20 World Cup Qualifier. Earlier in 2026, Norris represented MI London in the women’s Hundred. She took four wickets in six appearances, maintaining an economy rate of 7.83. At Mumbai Indians, Norris will reunite with head coach Luke Williams. She was part of Southern Brave in the 2021 edition of the Hundred, when Williams served as an assistant coach to Charlotte Edwards.MI complete overseas quota ahead of WPL 2027 auctionNorris’ signing completes Mumbai Indians’ overseas quota for the upcoming season. The franchise already has overseas players Amelia Kerr, Hayley Matthews, Nat Sciver-Brunt, Nicola Carey and Shabnim Ismail among its retained squad members, with Norris eligible to play as an additional overseas player because she represents an Associate nation. MI have retained 11 players ahead of the auction, including captain Harmanpreet Kaur, Amanjot Kaur, Sajeevan Sajana, Sanskriti Gupta, Rahila Firdous and Vaishnavi Sharma. The franchise released six players: G Kamalini, Saika Ishaque, Milly Illingworth, Kranthi Reddy, Poonam Khemnar and Triveni Vasistha. Mumbai Indians will enter the WPL 2027 auction with a purse of Rs 90 lakh and six slots to fill. The auction is scheduled to take place in Kochi on October 28.WPL 2027 schedule and auction detailsThe fifth edition of the Women’s Premier League will be held from January 14 to February 7, 2027, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced. The player retention deadline was set for September 28, with the five participating franchises required to finalise their retained players before the auction. The BCCI has yet to announce the host cities for the tournament. The WPL began in 2023 and will feature the same five franchises in its fifth season. Mumbai Indians have won two WPL titles in four seasons and will look to add to their trophy tally in 2027.

title: Tax evasion to Portugal fallout: Controversies that rocked Ronaldo's career
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were initiated following his departure from the national team camp
fullText: Cristiano Ronaldo will always be one of the names mentioned whenever there is a discussion about the best players in football history. The Portuguese forward holds the record for the highest number of goals scored in international football (146 goals) and the most career goals overall (980 goals).However, as legendary as his career has been, there has been no shortage of controversies that have followed him throughout his career. The latest entry on the list comes in the form of a provisional suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after he left the national team camp midway through the recently concluded leg of the UEFA Nations League.Ronaldo left the camp after a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus over his playing time and went on to issue a lengthy statement to the media criticising the coach, following which the Portuguese federation decided to take disciplinary action against him in the form of a provisional suspension while the incident is under investigation. The length of the suspension will be decided on the basis of the outcome of the investigation.With the latest verdict in place, let’s take a look at the major controversies Ronaldo has faced so far in his career, including those involving club and international football.Portugal national team suspension (2026)Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were initiated following his departure from the national team camp ahead of Portugal’s UEFA Nations League clash against Denmark earlier this month.The 41-year-old forward left the squad after a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus over his playing time. Ronaldo had been left on the bench against Norway and subsequently accused the coach of breaking promises regarding his involvement in the team.Ronaldo later apologised to his teammates and supporters, acknowledging that he should not have left the camp. He also called on the federation to punish him for his actions, saying he would accept whatever decision was made. However, he maintained that he wanted to continue representing Portugal.The FPF confirmed on October 10 that disciplinary proceedings had been initiated against Ronaldo following a decision by its Non-Professional Section on October 9. The case was referred to the federation’s Disciplinary Investigation Commission and designated as urgent.According to the federation, Ronaldo was initially subject to an automatic provisional suspension, followed by a further suspension as the disciplinary process progressed. The FPF did not announce a final punishment and said details of the proceedings would remain confidential until the investigation was completed.Ronaldo could face a suspension of between one and six months under the federation’s disciplinary regulations. The rules state that a player who abandons or fails to attend a national team training session, match or activity without justification can be suspended for that period, in addition to receiving a fine.Although Ronaldo informed the federation that he was leaving the camp, it remained unclear whether his departure would be considered justified under the regulations. Consequently, the potential six-month suspension remained a possible punishment rather than a confirmed verdict.ALSO READ: Ranji Trophy: Here's why Arunachal Pradesh forfeited their game vs NagalandAl-Nassr gesture towards Saudi fans and one-match ban (2024)Ronaldo was handed a one-match suspension by the Saudi Arabian Football Federation in February 2024 after making a gesture towards supporters following Al-Nassr’s 3-2 Saudi Pro League victory over Al-Shabab.During the match, sections of the crowd had chanted the name of Lionel Messi, Ronaldo’s long-time rival. After the final whistle, the Portuguese forward cupped his hand to his ear and made a gesture towards the supporters that attracted criticism.The Saudi federation’s disciplinary committee imposed a one-match ban and a financial penalty. The incident was another example of Ronaldo’s conduct outside the immediate action of a match becoming the subject of formal disciplinary scrutiny.Al-Hilal gesture controversy (2023)Ronaldo attracted criticism after Al-Nassr’s defeat against Al-Hilal in April 2023. As he left the pitch, he appeared to make a gesture towards his groin after supporters chanted Messi’s name.The footage circulated widely on social media, prompting criticism from sections of the Saudi public. Some commentators called for disciplinary action, while the incident also generated debate about the conduct expected of high-profile players in the Saudi Pro League.The episode did not result in the same widely reported formal suspension as the February 2024 incident. It nevertheless became one of the most discussed controversies of Ronaldo’s early period in Saudi Arabian football.Manchester United interview and contract termination (2022)Ronaldo’s second spell at Manchester United ended in November 2022 following an interview with broadcaster Piers Morgan. In the interview, the forward criticised the club’s leadership, questioned its direction and said he felt betrayed by people at Old Trafford.He also said he did not respect manager Erik ten Hag, with whom his relationship had deteriorated during the 2022-23 season. Ronaldo had struggled to secure a regular starting place under the Dutchman and had been involved in disagreements over his role in the team.Manchester United responded by announcing that they had initiated appropriate steps following the interview. The club subsequently confirmed that Ronaldo would leave with immediate effect by mutual agreement.Ronaldo said it was the right time to seek a new challenge and thanked the club and its supporters. He later joined Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr, bringing his second stint at Old Trafford to an abrupt end.Refusal to come on against Tottenham (2022)Ronaldo faced disciplinary action from Manchester United in October 2022 after refusing to come on as a substitute during the Premier League match against Tottenham Hotspur.United won the match 2-0 at Old Trafford, but Ronaldo’s conduct became a major talking point after he walked down the tunnel before the final whistle. Manager Erik ten Hag subsequently left the forward out of the squad for United’s next match against Chelsea.The incident followed a period in which Ronaldo had found himself outside the regular starting XI. Ten Hag maintained that players were expected to respect the team’s decisions and disciplinary standards, regardless of their stature.Ronaldo later returned to the squad, but the episode added to the tension surrounding his position at the club. The disagreement was also part of the wider breakdown in his relationship with United that culminated in the November interview and his departure.Knocking a fan’s phone after Everton defeat (2022)In April 2022, Ronaldo appeared to knock a mobile phone out of a young Everton supporter’s hand as he walked towards the tunnel following Manchester United’s 1-0 defeat at Goodison Park.Footage of the incident circulated on social media, prompting criticism of the forward’s behaviour. Ronaldo apologised publicly, describing his reaction as an outburst in a difficult moment, and invited the supporter to watch a match at Old Trafford.The incident was investigated by the Football Association. In November 2022, an independent disciplinary commission found Ronaldo guilty of improper and violent conduct. He was handed a two-match domestic suspension and fined £50,000.Ronaldo admitted the charge of improper conduct but did not admit the violent-conduct charge. He also received a police caution in connection with the incident.The suspension was announced shortly before the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar, although it did not affect his participation in the tournament. The case became another disciplinary issue in the closing months of his second spell at Manchester United.Spanish tax evasion case and settlement (2017–2019)Ronaldo’s legal troubles in Spain emerged from allegations concerning income generated through his image rights during his time at Real Madrid. Spanish prosecutors accused him of evading taxes on income earned between 2011 and 2014.The allegations centred on the use of companies and business structures outside Spain to handle income from commercial agreements. In 2017, prosecutors accused Ronaldo of having defrauded the Spanish state of approximately €14.7 million. Ronaldo denied knowingly committing tax evasion.In January 2019, he appeared before a Madrid court after reaching a settlement with Spanish authorities. Under the agreement, he accepted a fine of €18.8 million and a suspended prison sentence of 23 months.Under Spanish law, a first-time offender receiving a sentence of less than two years can generally avoid serving time in prison, subject to applicable conditions. Ronaldo therefore did not serve the prison sentence.The settlement brought the case to a conclusion but remained one of the most significant off-field controversies of his career. It also placed his commercial earnings and image-rights arrangements under international scrutiny.World Cup wink controversy involving Wayne Rooney (2006)Ronaldo became a central figure in one of the most memorable controversies of the 2006 FIFA World Cup during Portugal’s quarter-final against England.England forward Wayne Rooney was sent off after an incident involving Portugal defender Ricardo Carvalho. Ronaldo was seen gesturing towards the Portugal bench in the aftermath of the incident, and television footage captured him winking in the direction of his teammates.The moment prompted accusations from English supporters and sections of the media that Ronaldo had encouraged the referee to dismiss Rooney, who was then his teammate at Manchester United.The incident intensified the rivalry between the two players in the immediate aftermath of the match. Rooney initially expressed disappointment with Ronaldo’s involvement but later said he bore no ill feeling towards him.Portugal won the quarter-final on penalties after the match finished goalless following extra time. The episode became a lasting image of the tournament and generated considerable debate in England, particularly because Ronaldo and Rooney played for the same club.Although the incident did not result in a disciplinary sanction against Ronaldo, it placed him at the centre of an international football controversy early in his career.

title: Ranji Trophy: Here's why Arunachal Pradesh forfeited their game vs Nagaland
summary: The forfeiture follows Arunachal Pradesh's failure to field their Under-19 team for a Vinoo Mankad Trophy match against Sikkim in Bhubaneswar on Thursday
fullText: Arunachal Pradesh have forfeited their Ranji Trophy Plate Group opener against Nagaland, scheduled to begin in Ahmedabad on Sunday, amid an administrative crisis in the state cricket association.A dispute over the state cricket association's leadership and election process before the Itanagar bench of the Gauhati High Court have left the association without a functioning authority to make decisions on team selection, preventing the state from fielding a side for the domestic fixture.The forfeiture follows Arunachal Pradesh's failure to field their Under-19 team for a Vinoo Mankad Trophy match against Sikkim in Bhubaneswar on Thursday. The ongoing legal dispute has also prevented the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) from intervening in the association's affairs and constituting an independent selection panel.What is the dispute within the Arunachal Pradesh Cricket Association?The Arunachal Pradesh Cricket Association (APCA) held its elections in September, with Nabam Vivek elected as president. However, multiple district associations subsequently approached the Gauhati High Court, alleging irregularities in the election process.The dispute has left the association unable to function normally, with no authorised body in a position to make decisions regarding team selection. According to reports, players contracted to represent the state were also uncertain about whether they needed to report to Ahmedabad for the Ranji Trophy opener.The High Court has reserved its order in the matter, leaving the association's administrative arrangements unresolved. ALSO READ: Australia seize control of 1st Test against South Africa with 139-run leadWhy can the BCCI not intervene?The BCCI has been unable to appoint an independent selection panel or administrator to manage cricketing operations in Arunachal Pradesh because of the ongoing court proceedings and the restrictions on the association's functioning.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia had explained that the board could not intervene until the court provided clearance. He said the state body was not functioning and the BCCI could not make decisions while the matter remained before the court.The board had previously appointed committees to oversee cricketing operations in Bihar following a request from the Bihar Cricket Association. However, it has not been able to adopt a similar arrangement in Arunachal Pradesh because of the legal restrictions arising from the pending case.How has the dispute affected Arunachal Pradesh's domestic cricket?The administrative deadlock has affected both senior and age-group cricket in the state.Before forfeiting their Ranji Trophy opener against Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh failed to field their Under-19 team for a Vinoo Mankad Trophy match against Sikkim in Bhubaneswar on Thursday.The lack of an operational authority has prevented the association from making decisions on team selection and organising preparations for domestic fixtures. Reports also indicated that contracted players were awaiting clarity on their participation in the season.The dispute has therefore affected the state's ability to field teams across different levels of domestic cricket.What has Nabam Vivek said about the situation?Vivek has maintained that the association cannot field teams while the court restrictions remain in place. He has also said the BCCI has been informed about the circumstances surrounding the dispute.According to reports, Vivek argued that sending teams to compete without further directions from the court could amount to contempt of court. He maintained that the association was not in a position to participate in domestic competitions until an interim order or judgment clarified its position.The allegations concerning the election process remain before the court, and the dispute has not been resolved through a final judgment in the reports reviewed.How did Arunachal Pradesh perform in the previous Ranji Trophy season?Arunachal Pradesh finished at the bottom of the Plate Group standings in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season, losing all five of their matches.The team competes in the Plate Group alongside Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Sikkim.The forfeiture of the opening fixture against Nagaland comes as the state faces uncertainty over its participation in the ongoing domestic season. The status of its remaining fixtures will depend on developments in the legal proceedings and any subsequent decisions by the BCCI.

title: New Zealand announce ODI squad for India series; Test stars to leave early
summary: Due to the Test series that follows the white-ball games, the selectors have named a split squad, withdrawing red-ball specialists after the third match
fullText: Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, and Tim Seifert will make their return to New Zealand's ODI setup, while Rachin Ravindra returns from a shoulder injury for the upcoming five-match series against India beginning November 4.Due to the Test series that follows the white-ball games, the selectors have named a split squad, withdrawing red-ball specialists after the third match.The New Zealand selectors have split the squad into three groups, with only six players -- Mitchell Santner (captain), Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Jacob Duffy, Will Young, and Blair Tickner -- named for all five ODIs.Devon Conway, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, and Nathan Smith will feature exclusively in the first three matches starting with the game at Eden Park in Auckland.Following the third game, these Test specialists will leave the squad to prepare for the longer format in Wellington.To fill the vacancies for the final two ODIs, seven additional players -- including Finn Allen, Kristian Clarke, Matt Fisher, Lockie Ferguson, Mitch Hay, Nick Kelly, and Seifert -- will join the squad.The BLACKCAPS will look to build on their historic 2-1 ODI series triumph over India on Indian soil in January, their first-ever bilateral ODI series victory in the country.Allen and Ferguson last featured in an ODI in 2023, with Ferguson's previous appearance coming in the World Cup semifinal against India in Mumbai. Seifert last played an ODI around 18 months ago during New Zealand's home series against Pakistan.White-ball captain Mitchell Santner will lead the extended squad, which largely retains the core of the team that secured the landmark series win earlier this year.Ravindra, who was ruled out of New Zealand's T20I squad due to a shoulder injury, will return for the opening three ODIs.The squad will undergo a change midway through the series, with several players heading to Wellington after the third match to prepare for the upcoming Test series. Seven additional players will join the ODI squad for the final two games.The five-match series will conclude with the fourth and fifth ODIs.Head coach Rob Walter said the ODI series is very significant considering the 2027 ICC Men's World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia."First and foremost this is huge series for us, playing in front of our fans in full stadiums against a formidable Indian side," he said."With the ODI World Cup just one year away it's important for us to also view these matches as valuable preparation for that event."Bringing in seven players for the final ODIs allows us to test our depth and see how those players fare against a world-class side.He added, "Obviously every Test match is important for us in terms of championship points, which is why we're extracting some of that squad early for additional preparation before the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve on November 19." The Test squad for the two-match series against India will be announced in early November.New Zealand ODI squads for India series: (ODIs 1-3) Mitchell Santner (C) Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Tom Latham (WK), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner, Will Young (ODIs 4 & 5): Mitchell Santner (C), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Lockie Ferguson, Mitch Hay (WK), Nick Kelly, Tim Seifert (WK), Blair Tickner, Will Young.

title: Messi nets brace in first game since Argentina retirement as Miami win 4-0
summary: Luis Suarez also scored twice and German Berterame had two assists for Inter Miami, which snapped a five-match winless skid
fullText: Lionel Messi scored two goals to give him a league-leading 23 this season, and Inter Miami beat D.C. United 4-0.Luis Suarez also scored twice and German Berterame had two assists for Inter Miami, which snapped a five-match winless skid. Miami had four draws and one loss before Saturday's outburst.Four days after playing his farewell match that ended a 21-year tenure with the Argentine national team, Messi played the entire 90 minutes.The win was Miami's first since a 7-1 rout of CF Montreal on Aug. 29. It was also the first league win for new coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez, who took over Sept. 16.D.C. United is winless in its last five matches.Messi scored his first in the 47th minute after Suarez tallied twice in the first half to give Inter Miami a 2-0 lead at the break. Suarez centered a pass near the 6-yard box, where Messi retrieved it and tapped in a shot inside the right post.Inter Miami padded its lead when Messi struck again in the 60th minute. He received Rodrigo De Paul's pass, dribbled inside the large area and eluded two United defenders to beat goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.Inter Miami's first scoring threat resulted in Suarez's goal three minutes into the match. Suarez received Berterame's header and beat Johnson with a shot that landed inside the left post.Suarez made it 2-0 with his second goal in the 39th minute. Johnson deflected Messi's point-blank shot to an open Berterame, who fed Suarez with another header that he retrieved inside the 6-yard box. Suarez then tapped in a shot for his brace.
